svg.title: mote0 reading gcd.mote
svg.text: # gcd.mote: the greatest common divisor of two numbers
read only to pass over it

g.title: Line 1 is a comment: read, and nothing to do.
g.text: # gcd.mote: the greatest common divisor of two numbers

g.title: Line 2, read i: i is 6. i is new, so it goes into the table of names.
Line 3, read j: j is 4. j is new, so it goes in at the top: the table is a list, and a new name goes at its front.
Line 4: i != j is 6 != 4, true: into the loop's lines.
Line 5: i > j is 6 > 4, true: the lines after then run.
Line 6, i := i - j: each name found in the table by its letters; i is now 2.
Line 7, else: the then lines are done, so mote0 reads ahead past the else lines.
Line 8 is read only to pass over it: mote0 is looking for an end.
Line 9 is the end it was looking for: on to line 10.
Line 10, end of the while: back to line 4, whose condition is read again.
Line 4: i != j is 2 != 4, true: into the loop's lines.
Line 5: i > j is 2 > 4, false: mote0 reads ahead for the else.
Line 6 is read only to pass over it: mote0 is looking for an end or an else.
Line 7 is the else it was looking for: the lines after it run.
Line 8, j := j - i: each name found in the table by its letters; j is now 2.
Line 9, end of the if: on to the next line.
Line 10, end of the while: back to line 4, whose condition is read again.
Line 4: i != j is 2 != 2, false: mote0 reads ahead for the loop's end.
Line 5 starts an if inside, counted: the next end is that if's, not the one wanted.
Line 6 is read only to pass over it: mote0 is looking for an end.
Line 7 is read only to pass over it: mote0 is looking for an end.
Line 8 is read only to pass over it: mote0 is looking for an end.
Line 9 is the end of the block inside, counted off: still looking.
Line 10 is the end it was looking for: on to line 11.
Line 11, write i: prints 2. 25 lines read, for a program of 11.
